recipes.name: Potato Crunchy Tenders
ingredients_raw: 1 (7.6 ounce) package garlic flavored instant mashed potatoes

steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Meanwhile, beat together milk and egg in a shallow bowl. Stir together instant mashed potatoes, salt, and pepper in another shallow bowl.
Stir chicken tenders with milk mixture to coat thoroughly, then shake off excess milk and dip each tender into potato flakes.
Cook breaded tenders in hot oil until golden brown, 7 to 10 minutes. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate.

raw_recipe.headline: Potato Crunchy Tenders
raw_recipe.description: These potato crunchy tenders feature fried chicken fingers coated in garlic-flavored mashed potato flakes before frying, making a quick, easy meal.

review.reviewBody: This tastes great but I don't like frying so I baked it. It was great. I used instant loaded baked potatoes and added shredded cheddar cheese to mix. Covered the baking pan with a thin layer of olive oil. Placed coated chicken strips on pan bake on 350 degrees for 10 min then turn chicken over bake another 10 min. No frying and it was loved by the whole family.

Just tried these for the first time, they are possibly the best chicken tenders I have ever made. I used "Idahoan Roasted Garlic" mashed potato mix which is better tasting than many of the others. I ended up having enough to cover two lbs of meat, but they are so good that was fine with me. Next time I will cut the salt back to 1 & 1/2 teaspoon, but other than that I love these! Thank you for posting. :-)
PS I used a light olive oil, worked great.
**Update, just made for second time. Added 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder & 1/4 cup parmesan cheese to the flakes. They were even better. After removing chicken, you can pour the left over milk in the frying pan, add flour & make gravy. Yum.
Soak chicken in buttermilk overnight. Then shake off excess buttermilk, dredge in flour, then in egg and buttermilk and then in flavored potato flakes, and air fry.

These were my first attempt at chicken fingers and I just loved how they came out with the instant mashed potatoes. I added some butter to the oil for frying. I cut the milk down to 1 cup. My box of instant potatoes was 6.6 ounces with 2 packs in it so I used both but that was unnecessary, one would have been enough. I cut the salt down to 1 teaspoon and added 1/2 a teaspoon of cayenne to the mix and a 1/4 cup of grated parmesan. I floured, egg/milk mixture then potato flake mixture and I did let the breaded fingers sit for 15 to 20 minutes before frying and had no problem keeping the coating on.

Loved this! The only changes I made were I added 1/2 cup of Parmesan cheese and 1/4 teaspoon of garlic powder. I don’t particularly like to fry so I baked them at 350 degrees for 10 minutes each side, adding shredded cheese on top after flipping. Absolutely quick, easy, and amazing meal!!!

My husband is the cook, so I suggested he do what another person did was soak the chicken in buttermilk overnight and use it with the egg and buttermilk to dip it in after the flour and let me tell you soooo moist but the potato flakes were getting done too fast in the deep fryer so we had to finish baking it in the oven on air fry, it was just so light and fluffy and moist! We even froze some raw as my son is deployed and he's a chicken lover so I can't wait for him to try this when he returns home next month! I forgot we used plain potato flakes and added onion powder.
These are so good. Double coated and oven baked. I added garlic salt, onion powder. I will be making these again and diabete friendly

Great recipe and easily modified! There are a variety of ways to prepare this. But, the first thing I will note- cut the milk measurement down!! You'll end up with too much left over, just to be thrown out. I used 1 egg and only 3/4 cup of milk (plus or minus, as needed). I also added some additional seasonings/spices to the dry mix. A little bit of cayenne pepper can easily make this similar to buffalo style chicken strips! The spices for the dry mix just depend on your taste preference. I also have used flour instead of mashed potato mix (I think flour works better). If you are using mashed potato flakes- WATCH THE OIL TEMP! Too high, and they will burn before they are done cooking through. I prefer using the powdered garlic mashed potato mix, or 1 cup of flour- either one, I still add additional spices/seasonings for flavor. But as other reviewers have posted- DOUBLE DIP BEFORE FRYING!!! Start by coating the chicken in the dry mix. Transfer to liquid mix, dipping enough to coat it well in the liquid, then re-dip & coat it in the dry mix before placing it in the frying pan. This should ensure that all pieces are fully coated, less likely to burn and will remain 'crispy' instead of soggy or the coating falling off. 
This recipe also works well to cook pork, fish and even veggies! Great base recipe, easily adaptable! Thank you for sharing. :)

I just made these and they were fantastic! I had some regular instant potatoes and I added garlic salt and then some chili powder and paprika to kick it up some! Also double coated each piece. Great recipe!

These were FAN-FREAKIN-TASTIC! Seriously, we couldn't stop talking about how we won't make breaded chicken any other way! I think we perfected this recipe with such minor changes-left out the salt since the instant potatoes are usually high in salt & double coated the chicken (egg batter, potato, egg batter, potato). This helped the coating stick really well and used up all the batter ingredients! These had a nice crisp potato pancake-like coating, a thin layer of mashed potatoes and juicy chicken inside. Hands down a real keeper. In fact I'm going to make it again tonight with a different flavored potato package! And I think these would be perfect with a chicken gravy on top.

I made this and it was delicious. I didn't have packaged mashed potatoes, so I used a cup of potato flakes and added a tablespoon of garlic and 1/4 cup of Parmesan cheese. I also double breaded by dipping in flour before the milk mixture. I used just 1 cup of milk and while a lot was left over, it made the drenching easier. I might use a bit less next time, but not much.

I tried baking it as suggested by another reviewer. Took more than 10 minutes on each side & did not turn out crispy for me. Flavor was good, so I might try again with frying them. Either as the whole cooking method, or before finishing in the oven. Thank you for the recipe!
Came out great. I had regular instant potatoes so I added garlic powder to the mix. Taste and crispiness was great. I'll fix this again soon. Easy to make for a single guy

This was a great, easy, and quick recipe that is now the family's favorite fried chicken option. I made one change to the recipe, I coated the chicken in the dry mix, then the wet mix, then the dry mix one more time. Next time, may add cayenne pepper or Cajun spice.
Yummy yummy. Husband and I love it.
Amazing! I only added 1/3 cup of grated parmesan to the instant pot mix because we like that flavor with our chicken strips. Next time, I'm making double because they go wicked fast. Soooo good!
Too spicy with that much pepper. Definitely will use less next time.

I was out of eggs and milk. Added garlic and onion powder and salt to flakes because mine were plain. Next time I ll add Parmesan cheese. But I sprayed the chicken with Pam then dredged. I read if cooking in oven try melted butter first. That will be next time but came out great. Thanks for the recipe.
Very good came out perfect will make again
This turned out great!
